data.summary: The theme logic, pre-paint script, header box and unit tests are solid and QA passes. However, ThemeToggle is mounted twice (desktop and mobile) with independent state and nothing listens to the dispatched change event. A hidden instance can therefore apply a stale 'system' preference and override the user's explicit choice when the OS scheme changes. This breaks the explicit light/dark acceptance criteria and must be fixed.

findings.issue: Header renders two ThemeToggle instances (desktop and mobile), each with its own useState and no subscription to THEME_CHANGE_EVENT (which is dispatched but never listened to). After the user clicks one instance, the other keeps a stale theme. The stale instance's 'system' matchMedia listener stays active and re-applies 'system' on an OS scheme change, overriding the user's explicit light/dark choice. The stale instance also shows a wrong label and computes the next theme from the wrong value when clicked after a resize.
findings.suggestion: Keep instances in sync: listen for THEME_CHANGE_EVENT (and the 'storage' event) in a useEffect and call setTheme(event.detail). Alternatively, have the OS-change handler re-read getStoredTheme(localStorage) instead of using the closed-over state, so it can never apply a stale value.
findings.rule: Correctness: explicit theme must not be overridden when OS changes

findings.issue: Broad global overrides of utility classes such as .dark .bg-white and .dark .text-gray-900 apply to every element using them, including ones that intentionally set a contrasting colour (e.g. buttons or badges). They also diverge from Tailwind's dark: variant approach set up in this same change, and are a maintenance trap (the .border-t.border-gray-100 rule is redundant with .border-gray-100).
findings.suggestion: Prefer per-component dark: variants over time (as the developer's follow-up notes), and at least remove the redundant rule. Verify that no component relies on bg-white with light text.

findings.issue: State initialises to 'system' and is corrected only in an effect, so the icon and label flash 'System default' before showing the real stored preference. The ThemeToggle component logic (cycle plus persistence wiring) also has no test.
findings.suggestion: Use a lazy initialiser or read the root's data attribute to avoid the flash, and consider extracting the cycle-and-persist step into theme.js with a unit test.

architectureNotes: Theme logic is isolated in a pure, injectable lib/theme.js with a duplicated inline mirror in Layout.astro; the comment documenting the mirroring is good, but the two must be kept in sync manually.
Cross-instance state (two toggles) should use a single source of truth (event or storage).
positives: Pure, dependency-injected theme.js (storage, root and matchMedia injected) makes tests deterministic.
Pre-paint inline script avoids flash of wrong theme and tolerates throwing localStorage.
Header link class logic was deduplicated into isHome/isAbout/linkBase constants.
Tests cover the cycle, the resolve matrix, throwing storage and class application with helpers at end of file.
mustFixBeforeMerge: In ui/src/components/ThemeToggle.jsx, synchronise the multiple ThemeToggle instances (subscribe to THEME_CHANGE_EVENT/'storage', or re-read the stored theme in the OS-change handler) so a hidden instance can never re-apply a stale 'system' theme over the user's explicit light/dark choice.
